app.footer: aegis-space-med · Educational prototype, NASA Space Apps 2026. Not a medical device. Demonstration data.

about.title: About the data
about.camera: Real webcam and the MediaPipe Face Landmarker model running in this browser: face detection, eye state, blinks, closure duration and PERCLOS. Frames exist only in memory; they are never recorded, uploaded or stored.
about.simulated: Heart rate, SpO₂, blood pressure, temperature, respiration, glucose, sleep, radiation, exercise, schedule and history. Generated deterministically from the selected scenario. They are not data from real astronauts.
about.userReported: Your answers to the fatigue, mood, stress and symptom questionnaire.
about.localTest: Result of the reaction-time test taken on this device.
limits: Educational prototype to support observation. It is not a medical device and does not diagnose.
It does not infer emotions, stress, depression or illness from the face.
The camera does not measure sleep, SpO₂, blood pressure, temperature or glucose.
Detector thresholds are experimental parameters, not official NASA medical limits.
If no face is found or quality is too low, the value is shown as “Not available”, never as zero.

bloodPressure.label: Blood pressure

glucose.label: Glucose
glucose.what: Blood glucose in mg/dL. Secondary indicator.

sleep.label: Sleep
sleep.what: Hours of sleep in the last cycle, estimated by fictitious actigraphy.
sleep.note: The camera does not measure sleep. Real actigraphy would need a wearable.

perclos.label: PERCLOS
perclos.what: Percentage of valid time with the eyes almost closed (≥ 80 % reduction from your reference openness), excluding blinks shorter than 400 ms.
perclos.note: Rolling 1 and 5 min windows. Without enough coverage it shows “Not available”. It is not a drowsiness diagnosis.

blinkRate.label: Blinks per minute
blinkRate.what: Confirmed eye reopenings per minute of valid time.
blinkRate.note: There is no universal normal value: it depends on the task and the person.

closures.label: Closures
closures.what: Blink < 400 ms · prolonged closure 400–499 ms · long closure ≥ 500 ms.
closures.note: Experimental detector cut-offs, not medical thresholds or proof of microsleep.

ear.label: Eye openness (EAR)
ear.what: Eye Aspect Ratio: ratio between eye height and width from 6 facial landmarks, normalized with your calibration.

quality.label: Capture quality
quality.what: Combines FPS, face presence, eye visibility, head orientation and lighting.
quality.note: With insufficient quality, metrics switch to “Not available” and no alerts are raised.

yawn.label: Prolonged mouth openings
yawn.what: jawOpen coefficient held ≥ 1.5 s. It may indicate a yawn, but does not prove it.

radiation.label: Accumulated radiation
radiation.what: Illustrative accumulated dose in mSv for an interplanetary transit.
radiation.note: Illustrative value, not a dosimetric measurement.

exercise.label: Exercise
exercise.what: Minutes of exercise completed according to the schedule.

reaction.label: Reaction time
reaction.what: Short local test: tap as soon as the stimulus appears. Real result of your interaction.

control.linkSub: Everything is stored on board first and sent when there is a link. The spacecraft never waits for an answer.
control.logSub: What has been stored on this device and will travel to Earth.
control.delayNote: Real signal delay: up to 20 minutes each way between Earth and Mars (NASA HRP). Moon and Mars are a sped-up demo: here they take seconds.
control.reportsSub: Every minute a vitals summary is sent per crew member, plus every “How I feel”, every traffic-light change and every completed protocol. Without a link they are kept on board and travel at the next contact.
control.noReports: No reports in the outbox yet.
control.neverSent: Photos, video, face points, the face template and the PIN are never sent.

a.today: Today, day {{day}}, your readings are within your usual range: pulse {{hr}} beats per minute (normal for you is {{usual}}), blood oxygen {{spo2}} %, pressure {{bp}} mmHg and temperature {{temp}} °C. You slept {{sleep}} h. No active alerts.
a.todayAlerts: Today, day {{day}}: pulse {{hr}} beats per minute (normal for you is {{usual}}), oxygen {{spo2}} %, pressure {{bp}} mmHg, temperature {{temp}} °C and {{sleep}} h of sleep. There are {{count}} active alert(s): open them in Alerts to see what to do.
a.oxygen: Your blood oxygen is {{spo2}} %: the share of your blood that carries oxygen. NASA studies lack of oxygen (hypoxia) as one of the risks of spaceflight. If you are short of breath or dizzy, open Emergency.
a.radiation: You have accumulated {{total}} mSv on the trip, about {{daily}} mSv per day in this demo. Space radiation cannot be seen or felt: that is why it is measured and logged. NASA considers it one of the main hazards of a Mars mission.
a.sleepWeek: Over the last {{count}} nights you slept {{avg}} h on average. {{short}} night(s) were under 6 h. If you feel tired, log it in “How I feel”.
a.sleepWhy: On long missions, good sleep helps keep attention and mood. NASA notes that sleep loss, a disrupted body clock and work overload add up in isolation. I do not recommend medication or doses: for serious symptoms, open Emergency.
a.logSymptom: Sure. In “How I feel” you mark your symptoms and the app tells you which protocol to follow.
a.baseline: What is normal for you, from what the app has learned, is a pulse of {{hr}} beats per minute, from {{count}} readings: {{state}}. It only explains your data; alert thresholds do not change.
a.baselineNone: I have no readings of yours yet to learn what is normal for you. I will start after a few minutes of use.
a.unsafe: I do not recommend medication or doses. If you feel unwell, open Emergency and follow the protocol with your crewmate or medical officer.
a.unknown: I do not have that answer in the onboard library. Try one of the quick questions, or open “Hazards & guide”.
